Simulate data for a multispecies false-positive occupancy model

Source: R/simulate_fp_ms.R
simulate_fp_ms.Rd

Generates one dataset from known parameters for fp_occu_ms(): several species on the same sites, occasions, recorders and verified occasions, each with its own occupancy, true detection and false positives drawn from distributions of the community, as in the model. In development, as fp_occu_ms().

Usage

simulate_fp_ms(
  nspecies = 5,
  nsite = 100,
  nocc = 10,
  psi = 0.4,
  sd_psi = 1,
  b1 = -0.5,
  sd_b1 = 0.5,
  p11 = 0.5,
  sd_p11 = 0.5,
  p10 = 0.05,
  sd_gap = 0.3,
  a_bio = 0,
  r11 = 0.6,
  frac_verified = 0.3,
  nver = 3,
  sd_recorder = 0,
  nrec = 5,
  frac_confirmed = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

nspecies

Number of species.

nsite, nocc, frac_verified, nver, nrec, frac_confirmed

As in simulate_fp().

psi, b1

Community mean occupancy probability at the mean of x, and community mean slope on x.

sd_psi, sd_b1

Standard deviations among species of the logit of occupancy at the mean of x and of the slope.

p11, p10

True-detection and false-positive probabilities of the community (at the mean detection intercept and the median gap); p10 must be below p11.

sd_p11

Standard deviation among species of the true-detection intercept (logit scale).

sd_gap

Standard deviation among species of the log of the gap.

a_bio

Shared slope of true detection on bio.

r11

Detection probability of the verified method, below 1.

sd_recorder

Standard deviation of the recorder effects on true detection, shared by the species. 0 by default.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A list of class fp_sim_ms with data (an fp_data object with the species column species; species are named sp1, sp2, ...) and truth: pars, the generating values named as the output of fp_occu_ms() with occ = ~ x and det = ~ bio (community values and the values of each species, occ_x[sp1], ...); z, the latent states, a matrix of sites by species; and p10_bar, the false-positive rate of each species.

Details

The sites, the occupancy covariate x, the occasions with their covariates bio and aci, the recorders, and which occasions are verified (or checked, with frac_confirmed > 0) come from simulate_fp() and are shared by the species. Each species \(s\) then has occupancy intercept and slope on x \(\beta_s = \mu_\beta + \sigma_\beta z_s\), true-detection intercept \(\alpha_s = \alpha + \sigma_\alpha z_s\), and gap \(g_s = \mu_g \exp(\sigma_g z_s)\) between its true-detection and false-positive intercepts, with \(z_s\) standard normal, so that its false-positive rate is \(\mathrm{logit}^{-1} (\alpha_s - g_s)\). The slope of true detection on bio, the verified detection probability and the recorder effects are shared. Given these values, the detections of each species are drawn as in simulate.fp_occu().

See also

fp_occu_ms(), simulate_fp()

Examples

s <- simulate_fp_ms(nspecies = 4, nsite = 50, nocc = 8, seed = 1)
s
#> <fp_sim_ms> 4 species at 50 sites
#>  species occupancy    p10
#>      sp1      0.28 0.0459
#>      sp2      0.66 0.0450
#>      sp3      0.10 0.0893
#>      sp4      0.58 0.0200
#> <fp_data>
#>   sites:                  50
#>   automated occasions:    1600 (naive occupancy 0.62)
#>   species:                4
#>   verified sites:         13 (156 occasions; verified detections at 8 sites)
#>   site x species known occupied: 13
#>   recorders:              5
#>   site covariates:        x, w 
#>   observation covariates: bio, aci 
#>   by species:
#>  species occasions detections sites_detected naive_occ verified verified_det
#>      sp1       400         70             24      0.48       39            4
#>      sp2       400        101             35      0.70       39           14
#>      sp3       400         55             32      0.64       39            2
#>      sp4       400        104             33      0.66       39            4
